scenes.title: I.1 · Equilateral triangle on a line

beats.headline: Given the line AB
Circle with centre A, radius AB
Circle with centre B; they meet at C
Join CA and CB
CA = AB = BC: equilateral

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.1

scenes.title: I.2 · A line at a point equal to a given line

beats.headline: At A, place a line equal to BC
Join AB; build equilateral DAB
Circle B, radius BC, meets DB at G
Circle D, radius DG, meets DA at L
DL = DG; take equals away: AL = BC

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.2

scenes.title: I.3 · Cut off from the greater a part equal to the less

beats.headline: Given AB, the greater, and C, the less
By Prop. 2, place AD equal to C
Circle A, radius AD, cuts AB at E
AE = AD = C

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.3

scenes.title: I.4 · Side-angle-side congruence

beats.headline: Two triangles
AB = DE, AC = DF, angle A = angle D
Lay D on A and DE along AB
The angles agree, so F falls on C
EF coincides with BC: congruent

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.4

scenes.title: I.5 · Base angles of an isosceles triangle

beats.headline: Isosceles: AB = AC
Produce AB, AC to D, E
Take F on BD; cut off AG = AF
Join FC, GB: AFC and AGB congruent
Subtracting: angle ABC = angle ACB

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.5

scenes.title: I.6 · Equal base angles give equal sides

beats.headline: Angles at B and C are equal
Suppose AB greater; cut off DB = AC
Then DBC would equal ACB
The part equals the whole: absurd. AB = AC

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.6

scenes.title: I.7 · No second triangle with equal sides on the same base

beats.headline: On the base AB stand AC and BC
Could D give AD = AC and BD = BC?
D would have to lie on both circles
On this side they meet only at C

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.7

scenes.title: I.8 · Side-side-side congruence

beats.headline: Three sides equal, each to each
Lay EF upon BC
If D missed A, Prop. 7 would fail
D falls on A: the triangles agree

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.8

scenes.title: I.9 · Bisect an angle

beats.headline: Given the angle BAC
Circle about A: cut off AE = AD
On DE build the equilateral DEF
Join AF: angle BAF = angle FAC

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.9

scenes.title: I.10 · Bisect a line

beats.headline: Given the line AB
Build equilateral ABC (Prop. 1)
Bisect angle ACB by CD (Prop. 9)
By side-angle-side, AD = DB

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.10

scenes.title: I.11 · Perpendicular from a point on a line

beats.headline: A point C on the line AB
Circle about C: CD = CE
Build the equilateral DEF on DE
Join CF: the adjacent angles are right

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.11

scenes.title: I.12 · Perpendicular from a point off the line

beats.headline: A point C outside the line AB
Circle about C meets AB at G, E
Bisect GE at H (Prop. 10)
Join CH: it is perpendicular

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.12

scenes.title: I.13 · Adjacent angles make two right angles

beats.headline: The line AB stands on CD
It makes the angles CBA and ABD
Draw BE at right angles to CD
Together they equal two right angles

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.13

scenes.title: I.14 · Two right angles make a straight line

beats.headline: Angles CBA + ABD = two right angles
Suppose instead BE continued CB
Then ABE would equal ABD: absurd
So CB and BD are one straight line

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.14

scenes.anchor: If two right lines (AB, CD) inte
scenes.title: I.15 · Vertical angles are equal

beats.headline: Two lines cut at E
The angle AEC
AEC + CEB = two right = CEB + BED
Take away CEB: AEC = BED

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.15

scenes.title: I.16 · Exterior angle exceeds either remote interior angle

beats.headline: Produce BC to D
Bisect AC at E; make EF = BE
ABE ≅ CFE, so angle A = angle ECF
ACD exceeds ECF, that is, angle A

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.16

scenes.title: I.17 · Any two angles are less than two right angles

beats.headline: Angles B and C of the triangle
Exterior ACD exceeds B (Prop. 16)
B + ACB < ACD + ACB
and ACD + ACB = two right angles

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.17

scenes.title: I.18 · The greater side subtends the greater angle

beats.headline: AC is greater than AB
Cut off AD = AB and join BD
Angle ABD = angle ADB (Prop. 5)
ADB exceeds C, so angle B exceeds C

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.18

scenes.title: I.19 · The greater angle is subtended by the greater side

beats.headline: Angle B is greater than angle C
If AC = AB the angles would be equal
If AC < AB, B would be the less
Therefore AC is greater than AB

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.19

scenes.title: I.20 · Two sides are greater than the third

beats.headline: To show BA + AC > BC
Produce BA to D, AD = AC; join DC
Angle ADC = angle ACD
BCD is greater, so BD = BA + AC > BC

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.20

scenes.title: I.21 · Two lines drawn to a point within

beats.headline: The triangle ABC
From B and C draw lines to D within
Produce BD to E: BD + DC < BA + AC
but the angle BDC exceeds BAC

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.21

scenes.title: I.22 · A triangle from three given lines

beats.headline: Three lines, any two greater than the third
Take FG equal to c
Circles of radius a and b meet at K
KFG has sides a, b and c

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.22

scenes.title: I.23 · Copy an angle at a point

beats.headline: Angle DCE, and the point A on AB
Join DE to make the triangle CDE
Build AFG from the same sides (Prop. 22)
By Prop. 8, angle FAG = angle DCE

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.23

scenes.anchor: If two triangles (ABC, DEF) have two sides (AB, AC) of one respectively equal to two sides (DE, DF) of the other, bu
scenes.title: I.24 · The greater included angle has the greater base

beats.headline: Two sides equal, the angle at A greater
Place the other inside: AG = AC, base BG
Join CG: angle BGC exceeds BCG
Hence BC is greater than BG (Prop. 19)

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.24

scenes.anchor: If two triangles (ABC, DEF) have two sides (AB, AC) of one respectively equal to two sides (DE, DF) of the other, but the base (
scenes.title: I.25 · The greater base has the greater included angle

beats.headline: Two sides equal, and BC greater than BG
Equal angles would give equal bases
A smaller angle would give a smaller base
So the angle BAC is the greater

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.25

scenes.anchor: If two triangles (ABC, DEF) have two a
scenes.title: I.26 · Angle-side-angle congruence

beats.headline: Angle B = E, angle C = F
and the sides between them, BC = EF
If AB were greater, cut off GB = DE
Then GCB = ACB, absurd: congruent

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.26

scenes.title: I.27 · Equal alternate angles: the lines are parallel

beats.headline: The line EF falls on AB and CD
The alternate angles AEF, EFD are equal
Suppose the lines met when produced
Prop. 16 forbids it: they are parallel

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.27

scenes.anchor: If a right line (EF) intersecting two right lines (AB, CD) makes the exter
scenes.title: I.28 · Equal corresponding angles: the lines are parallel

beats.headline: EF cuts AB and CD
The angles GEB and EFD are equal
or BEF + EFD make two right angles
Alternate angles agree: parallel

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.28

scenes.anchor: If a right line (EF) intersect t
scenes.title: I.29 · Parallels make equal alternate angles (Postulate 5)

beats.headline: AB is parallel to CD; EF cuts both
If AEF were greater than EFD...
...then by Postulate 5 they would meet
So the alternate angles are equal

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.29

scenes.anchor: If two right lines (AB, CD) be p
scenes.title: I.30 · Lines parallel to the same line are parallel

beats.headline: AB and CD are both parallel to EF
Draw GK across all three
The angles are equal in turn (Prop. 29)
Hence AB is parallel to CD (Prop. 27)

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.30

scenes.title: I.31 · A parallel through a given point

beats.headline: Through A, draw a parallel to BC
Take D on BC and join AD
At A make DAF equal to ADB (Prop. 23)
Alternate angles agree: EF ∥ BC

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.31

scenes.title: I.32 · The angles of a triangle make two right angles

beats.headline: The three angles of a triangle
Produce BC; draw CE parallel to AB
Alternate angles: ACE = A
Corresponding angles: ECD = B
Together on one line: two right angles

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.32

scenes.title: I.33 · Joining equal and parallel lines

beats.headline: AB and CD are equal and parallel
Join AC and BD
Join BC: the triangles are congruent
So AC and BD are equal and parallel too

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.33

scenes.title: I.34 · Opposite sides and angles of a parallelogram

beats.headline: The parallelogram ABDC
Draw the diameter BC
The two triangles agree (Prop. 26)
Opposite sides, angles equal; BC halves it

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.34

scenes.title: I.35 · Parallelograms on the same base between the same parallels

beats.headline: Parallelogram ABCD on the base BC
Slide the top along the parallel
The triangle lost equals the one gained
The area is unchanged: they are equal

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.35

scenes.title: I.36 · Parallelograms on equal bases between the same parallels

beats.headline: BC = FG, between the same parallels
Join BE, CH: the parallelogram EBCH
ABCD = EBCH (Prop. 35)
EBCH = EFGH, so ABCD = EFGH

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.36

scenes.title: I.37 · Triangles on the same base between the same parallels

beats.headline: Triangle ABC, its vertex on the parallel
Move the vertex along the parallel...
...to D: the triangle DBC
Same base and height: equal areas

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.37

scenes.title: I.38 · Triangles on equal bases between the same parallels

beats.headline: Two triangles between the same parallels
with equal bases BC and EF
Each is half a parallelogram (Prop. 36)
So the triangles are equal

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.38

scenes.title: I.39 · Equal triangles on the same base are between parallels

beats.headline: ABC = DBC on the same base
To show AD is parallel to BC
Else the parallel meets BD at E
Then EBC = DBC, the part equal to the whole

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.39

scenes.title: I.40 · Equal triangles on equal bases are between parallels

beats.headline: Equal triangles on equal bases
Argue as in the previous proposition
So AD is parallel to BF

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.40

scenes.title: I.41 · A parallelogram is double the triangle

beats.headline: Parallelogram ABCD and triangle EBC
Join AC: ABC is half the parallelogram
ABC = EBC (Prop. 37)
So the parallelogram is double the triangle

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.41

scenes.title: I.42 · A parallelogram equal to a triangle

beats.headline: Given the triangle ABC and an angle
Bisect BC at E
Angle at E, parallel through A: FECG
FECG = twice AEC = ABC

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.42

scenes.title: I.43 · The complements about the diameter are equal

beats.headline: The parallelogram and its diameter AC
Through K on AC draw parallels to the sides
Two complements lie on either side of AC
Equal halves minus equal halves: equal

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.43

scenes.title: I.44 · Apply a parallelogram to a given line

beats.headline: Given AB, a triangle and an angle
First BEFG equal to the triangle (Prop. 42)
Complete the figure; draw the diameter HK
The complement ABML = BEFG (Prop. 43)

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.44

scenes.anchor: To construct a parallelogram equal to a given rect
scenes.title: I.45 · A parallelogram equal to any rectilineal figure

beats.headline: Any rectilineal figure ABCD
Divide it into triangles
The first becomes a parallelogram
Apply the second above it (Prop. 44)

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.45

scenes.title: I.46 · Describe a square on a line

beats.headline: Given the line AB
Erect a perpendicular at A; cut off AD = AB
Parallels through D and B meet at E
Equal sides, right angles: the square ADEB

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.46

scenes.title: I.47 · The square on the hypotenuse

beats.headline: A right triangle and its three squares
AL parallel to BD splits the great square
The triangle FBC...
...turns about B into ABD (Prop. 4)
Square BG = BL, CH = CL: sum = BE

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.47

scenes.title: I.48 · Converse of the Pythagorean theorem

beats.headline: Square on BC = squares on AB and AC
Draw AD at right angles to AC, equal to AB
Then DC² = AD² + AC² = BC², so DC = BC
By Prop. 8, the angle BAC is right

scenes.caption: Euclid, Elements I.48
